title: How to Make an End Turn Battle Command (and one extra question)

posts.author: funkyvibes
posts.body:
Getting to the point, I am trying to make a battle system like the RPG Panic at the Dojo and there are two elements I'm struggling to emulate. Apologies if I use the wrong terms or seem out of my depth, I'm new to Maker.
The first big one is an end turn feature. I would like to add one to my battle commands but no plugin I've found seems to let me do so. The Himeworks Actor Battle Command only lets me edit preexisting commands or add a skill as a command. I saw someone use Yanfly's Battle Command List plugin to add a "command execute" (
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/a-way-to-promptly-end-the-players-turn.75396/
) but that plugin is for Ace and I'm using RMMV.
I really need this command because I'm using Instant Cast on every skill to let players take as many actions as they need a turn, so they need to have the ability to end a turn on their own terms.
The second one is letting Armor and Weapons perform a "dice roll" for how much Mana an Actor gets at the start of the turn. I assume I can do some javascripting in the notes of either to make them choose a random number within a range and add that to the MP gauge. But I'd like someone to walk me through the best plugins to do so I don't brute force it.
(Oh and if you know how to make the MP icon look like a bunch of ticks, kind of like how ammo looks in some games, rather than a bar that'd be great so I don't come back in two days asking that. I'll include an image of what I mean.)
Thanks and I hope I did this thread thing right.

I have a somewhat similar mechanic where Actors have unlimited actions limited by their MP. What I do is give my actors a passive state that regens mana at the start of each turn. In your case, you could do it similarly and have a passive state that checks for specific armor and weapons, and then sets that actor's MP to the appropriate amount at the start of each turn.
Yanfly's BuffStateCore and AutoPassiveStates should be able to do that.
Someone who's much better at scripting can probably write up a script that does exactly that, but if nobody has done so by the time I have more time on my hands, I'll try to write one myself.

we're missing details here about your setup. im assuming that "End Turn" is a skill with high action speed so that it always goes first? if thats the case, then yes, immediately before that skill gets executed is the start of the turn.
The whole point of the instant actions is that theyre executed during the input phase, which is before the turn starts. if you want the MP regen to happen after the enemies act, then it cant be at the start of the turn. youd have to use something later like a <Custom Turn End Effect> or a <Custom Regenerate Effect>
Edit: also double check your state notetag. the actor lost MP on that second turn. is that intentional?

Unless you have a plugin that changes it, actors and enemies do their actions within the turn based on their AGI and action speed. actors do not always go first and enemies do not always go last unless the relevant calculations and comparisons makes it so. Before turns begin is an input phase for the player to select the actions their actors perform
funkyvibes said:
What you said about Instants is interesting and I'm wondering if you can elaborate so that I understand RMMV's battle system better.
Click to expand...
this is the reason why the normal recommendation is to make a small project to learn what the engine does before using plugins to alter it. Once youre familiar with the engine, understanding plugin changes becomes easier as plugin creators tend to use the same technical terms as the engine. From the Instant Cast plugin's introduction:
When an action has an instant cast property, that action is used immediately
on the spot
without needing to wait for the turn to start
.
Click to expand...
Instant actions for actors are executed during the Input phase immediately as the skill is chosen. they are done before the turn actually begins. An instant action taken by the player on the first turn for example, is done on turn 0 (just like turn 0 troop events). once the input phase is over does turn 1 begin.
